name: Shukeir–Hurghada Gas Pipeline

values.RouteType: Not mapped (but could be — route or endpoints are known)
values.RouteNotes: Endpoints known (Ras Shukeir on the Gulf of Suez to Hurghada) but no GIS geometry located; Red Sea west-coast corridor. Upstream of and physically distinct from P6034 (Hurghada–Safaga).

researcher_notes:
MATCH CHECK: distinct from P6034 (Hurghada–Safaga, 38.5 km, Hurghada→Safaga, operating). This candidate is Ras Shukeir→Hurghada (127 km) — the upstream Red Sea west-coast trunk that FEEDS Hurghada, whereas P6034 continues Hurghada→Safaga downstream. No existing GEM Egypt gas row covers the Ras Shukeir→Hurghada leg (checked all 57 existing rows incl. names/segments/other-names). Not P6034's parent-under-another-name. => new_row.

ADD-THRESHOLD (all three met): (a) sponsor = GASCO / Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Co; (b) endpoints = Egypt, Ras Shukeir (Gulf of Suez) → Hurghada (Red Sea Governorate); (c) concrete step = completed & operating since 2006.

CONFIDENCE = medium. Specs (127 km, 24 in, 7 MMcf/d, EGP 336 million, 2006) come from a SINGLE trade-press source (Oil & Gas Journal, Sept 2007), which attributes the work to Gasco — verified via url_verifier (200 + 'Shukeir' present) and confirmed verbatim: 'Also during 2006, Gasco completed the Shukeir-Hurgada pipeline, 127 km (79 miles) of 24 in. that can handle 7 MMcfd of gas for the Red Sea Governorate ... Estimated cost of the line was L.E. 336 million.' Existence + operator + Hurghada endpoint independently corroborated by GASCO's own site (Wayback 2020-07-30 capture of gasco.com.eg pipelines page, url_verifier OK + 'Hurghada' present): '...covering the west coast of the Red Sea reaching Hurghada city.' The GASCO page corroborates the line's existence/operator/endpoint but not the numeric specs, so the specs remain single-source (medium, not high).

OWNER: set to 'Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Co [100.%]' to match the exact convention on sibling row P6034 and other GASCO-operated Egyptian lines (GASCO is the EGAS transmission subsidiary named in OGJ). No 'Owner [ref]' column exists in this tracker CSV; per project convention owner/operator refs are staged on the separate operators/owners tab, so Owner is intentionally left without an inline [ref].

COST: OGJ states 'L.E. 336 million' (Egyptian pounds, 2006); staged as ProjectLevelCost=336, ProjectLevelCostUnits='EGP million' (no established Egypt-row precedent for the units string — flag for reviewer).

ROUTE: endpoints known, no GIS geometry located (searched EN + AR); RouteAccuracy='no route', RouteType='Not mapped (but could be...)'. Arabic searches surfaced the Ras Shukeir–Hurghada gas plant/port system (MISR Engineering, youm7) but no verifiable source adding independent pipeline specs.

SOURCE INDEPENDENCE CAVEAT: OGJ and GASCO both ultimately trace to Gasco for the existence claim; they are a primary (operator) + independent trade-journalism pairing rather than two fully independent chains, hence medium not high.
